extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, advocates, DHS adjudicators, and policymakers involved in public charge determinations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for how DHS will determine whether an applicant is likely at any time to become a public charge, including which benefits are countable, how past and current receipt are weighed, and the use of a totality-of-the-circumstances framework together with statutory minimum factors and the Affidavit of Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of public cash assistance for income maintenance and long-term institutionalization at government expense
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider current and/or past receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance and long-term institutionalization at government expense in public charge inadmissibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such receipt "will not alone be a sufficient basis" for a public charge finding; these items (which include SSI and TANF and State/Tribal/territorial/local cash benefit programs) are to be considered as part of the totality of the circumstances along with statutory minimum factors and a sufficient Affidavit of Support when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of Home- and Community-Based Services (HCBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: HCBS (Medicaid-funded home- and community-based services) are excluded from consideration in public charge inadmissibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS supported excluding HCBS because they help people live and work in the community and do not provide 'total care for basic needs' (they do not pay for room and board); DHS therefore excludes HCBS while continuing to consider long-term institutionalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only Medicaid-funded long-term institutionalization considered
rubrics_metrics.description: "Long-term institutionalization" is the only category of Medicaid-funded services that DHS will consider in public charge inadmissibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other Medicaid-funded services are not treated as countable long-term institutionalization for public charge purposes; DHS consulted with HHS in making this distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/characterization of long-term institutionalization
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS generally considers 'long-term institutionalization' to be characterized by uninterrupted, extended periods of stay in an institution (e.g., nursing home or mental health institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sporadic stays with discharge after each stay would not be considered long-term institutionalization; long-term institutionalization may include off-site trips/visits without discharge. The term excludes imprisonment for conviction of a crime and institutionalization for short periods or for rehabilitation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term rehabilitation services are not countable
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term rehabilitation services should not be considered for public charge purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows the 1999 Interim Field Guidance; DHS reiterates that short-term rehabilitation services are excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of the circumstances framework
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will apply a 'totality of the circumstances' approach when making public charge inadmissibility determinations, considering statutory minimum factors, the Affidavit of Support when required, and current/past receipt of certain benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No single factor (other than lack of a sufficient Affidavit of Support where required) should be the sole criterion for determining likelihood of becoming a public charge; determinations must be individualized and based on the evidence presented in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of statutory minimum factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers will consider the statutory minimum factors designated by Congress (the rule references 'the five statutory minimum factors') as part of the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimum factors are considered together with the Affidavit of Support (when required) and countable past/current benefits; DHS will not separately codify specific weights for each factor in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support (Section 213A) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A sufficient Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA is treated as part of the analysis and, where required, lack of a legally sufficient affidavit can be outcome-determinative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule emphasizes the centrality of a sufficient Affidavit of Support when required and states that apart from lack of a sufficient affidavit, no single factor should be determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount, duration, and recency of benefit receipt must be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider the amount, duration, and recency of receipt of public benefits when assessing whether past or current receipt indicates likely primary dependence on government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are explicitly called out in the regulatory text as evidence elements to be weighed under the totality framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: No arbitrary look‑back/time window for past benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not impose an arbitrary fixed time frame (e.g., a five‑year window) for past benefit usage to be considered in public charge determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of a fixed window, DHS will evaluate past use under the totality of the circumstances, taking amount/duration/recency and other statutory factors into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and classes not subject to public charge consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain classes of individuals are exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility or eligible for waivers; DHS identifies categories (e.g., VAWA self‑petitioners, refugees) and references 8 CFR 212.23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS clarifies who is exempted from 212(a)(4) and also identifies groups excluded from consideration of receipt of certain public benefits (for example, those granted refugee benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Past benefit receipt remains relevant but not determinative; changed circumstances considered
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider past receipt of benefits (including past long-term institutionalization) as part of the totality of circumstances, but recognizes past receipt is not determinative of future use and will consider changes in circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant previously relied on benefits but now has stable employment or other changed circumstances, those facts will be weighed on a case‑by‑case basis along with other statutory factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to demonstrate institutionalization violated Federal law
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will have a meaningful opportunity to provide evidence that their current or past institutionalization violated Federal law (e.g., ADA or Rehabilitation Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS expects applicants to be able to submit such evidence so that adjudicators do not rely on institutionalization that may have been unlawful; institutionalization that violated Federal law is not automatically countable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race and country of origin prohibited as factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Race and country of origin should never be considered in a public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS agrees with commenters that race and country of origin must not be included and has not included them as factors to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waivers may be in the record and thus may be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the initial application (Form I-485 and accompanying questions) does not ask about fee waivers, DHS may consider evidence in the record that a noncitizen previously applied for or received a fee waiver as part of the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS declined to categorically exclude fee waiver requests/receipts from consideration because totality-of-the-circumstances analysis can encompass all evidence in the record that is relevant to the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes and tax documents as evidence of assets/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: While paying taxes is not a statutory minimum factor, taxpayers may submit tax documents to provide evidence of income, assets, or financial status; DHS may also consider evidence of failure to file taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will not require specific evidence beyond the questions on Form I-485 for adjustment applicants, but may consider tax evidence if offered as relevant to assets/resources/financial status.

rubrics_metrics.name: No presumption of heavy weighting for specific factors (reject 2019 heavily weighted framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule rejects the 2019 Final Rule's codification of specific 'heavily weighted' negative and positive factors and will not assign particular preordained weights to factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS found the 2019 approach unduly prescriptive and inconsistent with an individualized totality analysis; relative weight of each factor is determined by specific facts in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: No special negative weight for children or disability/health conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule eliminates provisions that previously gave extra negative weight to children under 18 or to an individual's disability or health condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS agrees such additional weights were discriminatory and inappropriate; factors should be weighed based on case‑specific evidence rather than categorical weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle to exclude benefits less indicative of primary dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will exclude consideration of benefits that are less indicative of primary dependence on government or for which applicants are likely ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule aims to focus on benefits most indicative of primary dependence while not unnecessarily chilling access to public programs that Congress has made available for health and well‑being.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS may periodically issue guidance and empirical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS may periodically issue additional guidance to help officers determine how different factors may affect likelihood of becoming a public charge, including empirical analysis of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such guidance would be intended to assist adjudicators without codifying rigid weights or unduly prescriptive evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of institutionalization across all levels of government
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider long-term institutionalization at government expense regardless of level of government (federal, state, local) as evidence of primary dependence for subsistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes institutions generally assume total care of basic living requirements (including room and board), and such institutionalization is relevant to the public charge inquiry when judged within the totality of circumstances.
